task: Exercise ABI-v9 Section 2 with source-free Fast Debug execution.
observation: The existing ABI tamper fixtures changed Section 1 while leaving Section 2 bound to the old digest and handler-arm inventory. Strict cross-section validation therefore stopped before the fixture's intended Section 1 diagnostic. A shared fixture helper now rebinds the section hash/digest and mirrors handler-arm counts; the source-free ABI, imported-effects, and forgery regressions pass without relaxing the production reader.
impact: Keeping adversarial fixtures internally consistent preserves fail-closed validation while still testing the intended malformed-Section-1 cases.

resolution.summary: Synthetic artifact helpers now update the paired Section 2 framing and handler-arm inventory.

tool_used: ABI-v9 test scripts and source-free Fast Debug

task: Exercise Fast Debug using the package check-only ABI-v9 interface.
observation: Margo check-only correctly writes ABI-v9 .mossi execution bodies without an rlib, but Fast Debug still required the native provider artifact while loading that complete interface. The interpreter path now skips native-artifact binding and relies on the checked Section 2 plus source-freshness/digest validation. The X1 fixture asserts check-debug emits no rlib and matches native-profile output and normalized trace events.
impact: A package can use its checked execution-body interface for Fast Debug before any native build, matching the check-only snapshot contract.

resolution.summary: Fast Debug no longer requires an rlib when it consumes a complete ABI-v9 Section 2.

task: Separate semantic imports from execution-body admission.
observation: Section 2 was excluded from package interface hashes but the common module loader still parsed and projected it for ordinary semantic imports. That meant an execution-body-only corruption could invalidate `moss check` without changing a downstream fingerprint. The loader now parses Section 1 for semantic imports and requests Section 2 only for Fast Debug; a regression confirms semantic acceptance and execution rejection for a corrupted Section 2.
impact: Semantic verdicts now depend only on Section 1, consistent with G1 fingerprints and checkstop; Fast Debug remains fail-closed on execution-body integrity.

resolution.summary: Module loading now has an explicit execution-body admission mode, used by Fast Debug only.

tool_used: moss check, moss run --interp, and Phase 26.1 G1/F1 gates

task: Implement entry-scoped Fast Debug and run X0 selected-entry work counters against .mossi providers.
observation: Test-mode project discovery originally loaded only test files, so a selected test that called a root-package API failed name resolution. Fast Debug now loads the package source universe and applies selected-test scope before checking. The X0 work counters also showed that imported non-generic bodies are snapshot inputs, not functions rechecked by the consumer; the enforced identity targets now count the reached consumer wrappers while dependency rebuilds and artifacts are reported separately.
impact: The checker has the declarations needed to resolve selected test calls without widening checked body scope, and X0 counts align with R8/R11 snapshot ownership.

resolution.summary: Fast Debug indexes package source and prunes to selected entries; enforced package-perf targets pass with .mossi dependency paths.

tool_used: moss-opt, margo debug/test --interp, and enforced package-perf

task: Verify native build/test agreement for implicit-root dependency imports.
observation: `margo build --check` and Fast Debug accepted an implicit root import from a dependency interface, while native `margo build` rejected the same reachable import as an unknown identifier. Native package analysis only enabled compiled-interface lookup for explicit modules. Enabling lookup when Margo supplies `MOSS_MODULE_PATH` makes the focused implicit-root fixture pass native build and test; direct `moss check` accepts with the provider path and rejects without it.
impact: The check-only verdict now agrees with native package compilation for this dependency import, and the fixture guards both the package commands and the required module-path boundary.
evidence: moss check <implicit main> --json with and without MOSS_MODULE_PATH

resolution.summary: Native package analysis now resolves imported compiled interfaces whenever Margo provides a module path; focused X2 native build/test and module-path verdict assertions pass. Corpus C1 and full-suite review remain pending.

tool_used: Margo build/test, moss check, Fast Debug, and C1 scope corpus gate
